messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — SLO breach detected: router.tail_latency.p99 >= 1200ms in eu-west-1. Streaming stalls and increased error rate on /v1/stream. Auto-page triggered. :rotating_light:
eli.oncall: on it. seeing alerts in datadog — p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.3s. is this global or regional?
maya.router-sre: regional. heatmap shows concentrated spikes for eu-west-1 shard set: shard-11, shard-12. a bunch of requests routed to cpu-backed fallback nodes causing tokenization stalls.
eli.oncall: any recent rollouts to routing policy?
maya.router-sre: yes — weight rollout v2.4.3 to prefer_local routing. diff looks suspicious: a policy generator produced a zero weight for neighbor affinity for shard-12. quick snippet: ```json
{"route_policy":"prefer_local","weights":{"shard-11":0.0,"shard-12":0.0,"fallback":1.0}}
```
maya.router-sre: that effectively pushed traffic to fallback pool which is cpu and overloaded. causes long-tail tokenization + streaming stalls.
jake.infra: can we flip fallback off or increase dedicated pool capacity as quick mitigation?
eli.oncall: prefer quick config change rather than scale — emergency rollback policy or bump shard weight. who has perm to update routing seeds?
maya.router-sre: i can update routing table. plan: set explicit weights for shard-12=0.6, shard-11=0.4, fallback=0.0; apply as hotfix. curl command to apply: ```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-admin.redwood/v1/routing/update -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"shard_weights": {"shard-11":0.4, "shard-12":0.6, "fallback":0.0}}'
```
eli.oncall: do it and report results. tagging @ana.support to track customer impact.
maya.router-sre: applying now. response: 200 OK. pushed config version routing-v2.4.3-hotfix-1.
eli.oncall: rolling metrics — p95 down to 300ms after ~60s, p99 trending -> 430ms. :thumbsup:
nana.support: FYI — we already received 3 customer tickets mentioning streaming stalls in eu-west-1, two are enterprise customers with long-lived sessions. sample ticket snippet: "sessions stall around token 120, then reconnects cause partial outputs". customers impacted ~0.4% of total requests in region, but heavy for streaming UX.
raj.product: please prepare a short customer-facing note. is there data on which models or endpoints hit the faulty shards?
maya.router-sre: looks correlated to large-context streaming sessions (seq_len > 2048), and reranking endpoints that pin to shard-12 for affinity. count query: `SELECT count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE region='eu-west-1' AND shard='shard-12' AND seq_len>2048 AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour'` -> ~6.2k reqs, ~3.1k streams.
eli.oncall: livepage? we should move to oncall bridge for 15 min to check rollback behavior and confirm customers recover. i'm starting a live bridge.
incident-bot: livebridge created: https://meet.redwood.live/bridge/1738054321 — incident channel pinned.
maya.router-sre: also seeing a secondary issue: routing seed generator intermittently wrote empty weight arrays during canary -> causes transient misassignment when seed refresh happens. root cause likely validation bug in the rollout orchestrator. storing as follow-up.
jake.infra: as a precaution i enabled autoscale for dedicated pool in eu-west-1 for 10 minutes (policy: +30% cap) — should smooth any residual fallback load.
eli.oncall: good. will monitor for 10m, then gradually step down. handoff: i'm oncall for 30m more, then handing to @maya.router-sre.
maya.router-sre: i'll take the 2nd half. follow-ups: create a postmortem entry, include timeline, config diffs, and suggest pre-apply validation that rejects zero-sum weight sets.
nana.support: notified affected customers via status page draft. will send targeted messages to the two enterprise contacts after we confirm stabilization.
eli.oncall: metrics update at +10m: p95=280ms, p99=410ms, streaming error-rate back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated but keeping bridge open for monitoring.
raj.product: add note to roadmap: route policy validation + safer canary expt. and flag for ops-runbook.
maya.router-sre: committing a hotfix patch to orchestrator: reject empty weight arrays and log full diff. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/router-orchestrator/pulls/4227
eli.oncall: creating incident record with initial notes. will assign to maya and infra for full RCA. tagging eng-sre for postmortem notification.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated). duration: 47 minutes. severity: Sev2. Postmortem required within 72 hours.
eli.oncall: thanks team. keeping notes in the bridge and will handoff to maya in 25m. any outstanding asks?
maya.router-sre: one ask: replay routing seed refresh in staging with canary enabled to reproduce and validate fix. will schedule.
nana.support: I'll follow up with customers and attach logs and timeline.
eli.oncall: closing slack thread for now, continuing details in postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
